problems.title: Umbra and penumbra
problems.statement: As you know, on clear sunny days, objects usually give rise to umbras and penumbras. Nowadays, the angle of the ecliptic plane to the celestial equator is $\varepsilon_0=23^\circ26.2'$ and is reduced by about $\upsilon=0.78'$ per century. Calculate in what century begins the period or in what century the period has ended when from the exactly vertical column located in Ashulia

Draw pictures explaining your solution.

problems.title: Star setting
problems.statement: The Bengal Tiger likes to observe stars. According to his calculations, some star will rise today at $19^{\rm h}45^{\rm m}$ and will culminate at $21^{\rm h}49^{\rm m}$. At what time yesterday did the star set? The refraction and horizon lowering can be disregarded. The solution has to include an artistic picture with an image of the Bengal Tiger-astronomer observing the star.

solution.incompleteReason: No official solutions are present in the inspected APAO 2015 archive.

problems.title: Comet Lovejoy
problems.statement:
The table below presents data for the comet C/2014 Q2 (Lovejoy), which this year was the brightest comet in our sky:

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery date | 17 August 2014 |
| Discovered by | Terry Lovejoy (Brisben, Australia) |
| Discovered with | 20-cm Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope |
| Perihelion ($q$) | 1.2904 au |
| Eccentricity | 0.99811 |
| Orbital period ($P$) | ~9000 years |
| Inclination | $80.301^\circ$ |
| Last perihelion | 30 January 2015 |
| Minimum magnitude | 3.9 mag |
| In constellation | Eridanus |
| Actual magnitude | 18.6 mag |
| In constellation | Hercules |

From these data, calculate in the easiest way, the approximate speed of the comet on January 30, 2015. The orbital speed of the Earth is $V_E\approx29.8$ km/s.

problems.title: Distance between galaxies
problems.statement: According to estimations of scientists, there are about 1800 galaxies in the cluster of galaxies in the constellation Coma Berenices, which show redshift of 0.023. The region in our sky covered by this cluster is about $9^\circ\times10^\circ$. Estimate the average distance between the galaxies in this cluster. Draw a picture explaining your solution.

problems.title: Cluster
problems.statement: Astronomers find a “star” which position in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is about 9 mag higher than the corresponding stars of the main sequence. Assuming the “star” was a cluster of stars similar to each other, estimate the number of stars in the cluster.

problems.title: Photons
problems.statement: Radio- (operating wavelength is about 21 cm) and optical (operating in the light visible to the naked eye) telescopes have been used to study one astrophysical object. It was discovered that the energy fluxes from the object in the radio and optical frequencies were equal.

parts.statement: Which photons’ number is the largest, radio or optical? (Write in English “radio” or “optical” respectively.) By how many times is it more?
What should be the size of the radio telescope to make its resolving power the same as that of the human eye?
